sources.title: Zocdoc Pay-Per-Booking for Providers: Fees & Cancellations
sources.span: A one-time booking fee applies only when a new patient books; the amount varies by specialty and location. Practices can set a monthly spend cap and pause spend at any time. If a patient cancels within 24 hours of booking the fee may be waived in good faith; practices may submit a claim within 7 days if a patient booked as new but had previously been seen.
sources.span_locator: sections on when fees apply, cancellations, and spend controls

sources.title: Zocdoc for Providers | Get More New Patients
sources.span: Marketplace listing, Sponsored Results, an AI phone assistant branded 'Zo', website scheduling, telehealth, intake forms, reminders, reviews and reporting. Self-reported scale: 250k+ providers, 200+ specialties, 175+ EHR/PMS integrations, 50 states. Named partners include Privia Health, Carbon Health, Wellstar Health System, Dental Care Alliance. Tiers: free basic, per-booking growth, advanced at $250 per provider/month plus booking fees.
sources.span_locator: provider overview, product modules, scale counters, pricing tiers

sources.title: Zocdoc
sources.span: Founded 2007 in New York City; free to patients while doctors pay to advertise appointment slots. Business model changed in January 2019 from provider subscriptions to a per-booking referral fee in some markets, with reported provider concern about recouping costs.

sources.title: ZocDoc Patient and Provider Complaints
sources.span: Recurring themes: providers shown as in-network who are not; appointments confirmed then cancelled shortly before the visit; offices unaware of the booking; providers charged per booking regardless of no-show. Verbatim fragments include 'Why would ZocDoc state you are in my network if you are not?' (Oct 2018) and 'Appointment was cancelled, giving no reason' (Oct 2022).

sources.title: Zocdoc | BBB Customer Reviews
sources.span: Page reports 4.89/5 across 3,042 reviews; visible entries dated 2026-07-11 to 2026-07-21 and uniformly positive. Recurring patient language centres on speed and ease: 'incredibly easy to book, reschedule, or cancel appointments', 'quicker appointment times', 'got an appointment that quick and with choices'.
sources.span_locator: rating header and most-recent review entries

sources.title: Should you use ZocDoc for your private practice?
sources.span: Practising clinician's assessment: per-booking fee varies by state and 'may be close to $70'; the fee is charged 'whether or not the client arrives or doesn't'. Frames the decision as whether marketplace bookings convert to consistent clients and whether the fee survives cancellations; concludes it is 'not a one and done solution to filling your practice'.

sources.title: Zocdoc Competitors for Dental Providers: The 2026 Alternatives Guide
sources.span: Names an alternative set: Opencare, 1-800-Dentist, Solv, LocalMed, NexHealth, Weave, Modento, Dental Intelligence, Google Business Profile, Yelp Reservations, Healthgrades, Vitals.com. Frames the practice decision around three questions: 'What is your average new-patient lifetime value?', 'How much capacity do you actually have to fill?', 'Where are you losing today?' Benchmark phrase: 'lowest blended cost per new patient'.

sources.title: Is Zocdoc Worth It? Pricing, Features & Best Alternative in 2026
sources.span: States a per-new-patient range of '$35 and $110' varying by specialty and region, and lists as drawbacks that 'fees are not listed until late in the sign-up process', that last-minute cancellations create revenue gaps, and that pricing varies unpredictably by specialty, region and competition. Publisher sells a competing scheduling product.

sources.title: Zocdoc Now Powers Real-Time Appointment Booking for Patients on Yelp
sources.span: Patients can go from searching for a doctor on Yelp to booking, via 'Book now' on business pages or 'Book appointment' in Yelp Assistant, to 'view real-time, in-network availability and schedule appointments instantly'. Launched on Yelp iOS; Android and desktop planned later in 2026.

sources.title: Zocdoc Launches The AI-Informed Patient Report
sources.span: Censuswide surveyed 1,186 U.S. adults and 1,000 U.S. healthcare providers in February 2026. Reported: 26% of patients have used AI to ask health-related questions; 23% have hidden that use from a doctor; 85% of providers report seeing more AI-informed patients over the past year; 83% have corrected AI-derived misinformation in a visit.

sources.title: Secret Shopper Study: Ghost Networks in Medicare Advantage Mental Health Directories
sources.span: Staff called 120 systematically selected in-network mental health provider listings across 12 plans in 6 states. 33% of listings were inaccurate, non-working numbers, or unreturned calls; more than 80% of contacted listed providers were unreachable, not accepting new patients, or not in network.

sources.title: Getting mental health therapists is so freaking difficult
sources.span: Verbatim care-seeker language: 'All therapists are either full or have these weird ass times'; 'Insurance portals just dont have updated contact details'; 'Most of the therapists don't return the call and have full voicemails'; 'Unable to find a free moment to make these constant follow up calls'.

sources.title: Search-result composition for same-day / no-referral / self-pay booking queries
sources.publisher: Web search engine result page (proxy observation)
sources.span: Query 'how to book a doctor appointment online same day without insurance card specialist referral' returns a result set dominated by self-pay telehealth (Sesame, Doctor On Demand), no-referral specialist booking (UberDoc), and health-system same-day pages (Mount Sinai, Sutter). Indicates a live query cluster around same-day access, referral requirements, and price-before-booking.
